item.title: EMERGENCY PROGRAMME COORDINATOR
item.description:
Country: Yemen
Organization: Action contre la Faim France
Closing date: 22 Oct 2026

About : Action contre la Faim

Created in 1979, Action contre la Faim is a non-governmental organization that fights against hunger. Its charter of humanitarian principals- independence, neutrality, non-discrimination, free and direct access to victims, professionalism, transparency - has been part of its identity for 45 years. Its mission is to save lives by eliminating hunger through the prevention, detection and treatment of under-nutrition, particularly during and after emergency situations linked to conflicts or natural disasters. Action contre la Faim focuses its actions on 7 main areas of expertise: Nutrition and Health - Mental Health, Psychosocial Support - Food Security and Livelihoods - Water, Sanitation and Hygiene - Advocacy - Climate - Research. In 2024, Action contre la Faim provided aid to more than 26 million people in 57 countries worldwide. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Under the supervision of the Deputy Country Director for Programmes, your mission will be to strengthen the country office's emergency preparedness and response capacities to ensure timely, effective, and coordinated emergency responses, and lead the implementation of emergency responses across all areas of intervention of ACF in Yemen.
The main responsibilities and challenges of the position will be as follows:
Strengthen and operationalize the country office's emergency preparedness and response system to ensure readiness for emergenciesDevelop and maintain up to date emergency preparedness and contingency plans
Design, maintain up to date and lead the implementation of emergency response standard operating procedures in line with ACF programme, finance, logistics, human resources, and security policies and procedures
Lead and coordinate emergency responses implemented by the country office to ensure providing timely and quality humanitarian assistance to populations affected by crisesEnsure continuous monitoring and analysis of the humanitarian, political, and operational context to identify emerging risks and response opportunities
Lead the activation of emergency responses in line with ACF's procedures and agreed decision-making mechanisms
Strengthen ACF's engagement with donors, partners, and through coordination mechanisms to enhance ACF's emergency positioning and resource mobilization capacityMonitor key humanitarian developments, donor priorities, and funding opportunities relevant to emergency preparedness and response
Represent ACF in humanitarian coordination fora: clusters, working groups and inter-agency fora etc.
Promote ACF's emergency response capacities, experience, and strategic priorities to external stakeholders (donors, partners etc.)

Profile :

You hold a Master's Degree in International relations/humanitarian work or any other related field.
You have at least 5 years of professional experience in the humanitarian sector, with a minimum of 3 years managing emergency response programmes.
You demonstrate a strong leadership and decision-making abilities, good communication, representation, and negotiation skills. You are recognised for your ability to work effectively under pressure and adapt to changing circumstances.
You master English (written and spoken)
Having a previous experience in Yemen is an asset.

Conditions d'emploi

Fixed term contract under French legislation: 6 months
Monthly gross salary from 2597 to 2968euros upon experience, including 13th month
Reimbursement of the pension insurance for non-French citizens: 16% of the gross monthly salary
Annual salary increase: 6% increase after and each 12 months of continuous contract
Monthly per diem and living allowance: 730 USD net, field paid
Monthly country allowance: 450euros
Child allowance: 1500euros per year per child present in the country of origin (maximum 6000euros/year)
Transportation and accommodation: Coverage of transportation costs and guest house
Medical coverage: ACF covers 100% of the health and repatriation insurance agreement fees, for your medical expenses (as well as your dependents if you have a family post), and up to 1 month after the end of your contract.
Salary sustainment measures (sickness, paternity, maternity)
Leaves and RnR: 25 days of paid leaves per year, 20 RnR per year, airfare reimbursement with a ceiling to get to the chosen break destination, and 215 euros for each RnR period
Accompaniment and trainings:Follow-up and support for career development
Free and unlimited access to the e-learning platform Talentsoft
ACF is committed to people with disabilities and actively fights against all forms of discrimination.

item.title: CHEFFE OU CHEF DE PROJET FINANCE SI - FRANCE
item.description:
Country: France
Organization: Action contre la Faim France
Closing date: 22 Oct 2026

About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Sous la supervision du Responsable de Service Outils, Formation et Projets, votre mission sera de garantir le développement et les évolutions nécessaires des Système de Gestion relatif aux Finances, dans le respect du cadre de gestion dicté par les services de la DAF.
Plus particulièrement, vos missions seront de:
- Coordonner l'évolution des Systèmes de Gestion Financière (SGF) existants
- Contribuer à la maintenance évolutive de l'ERP Finance
- Participer aux projets de transformation des outils finances En lien avec le responsable, contribuer aux études et projets
- Communiquer l'état d'avancement des évolutions auprès de toutes les parties prenantes
- Participer aux projets transversaux

Profile :

Vous êtes titulaire d'une formation supérieure en gestion financière, et vous avez au moins 3 ans d'expériences en gestion fonctionnelle de projet SI finance.
Vous avez des compétences techniques dans les domaines suivantes : cycles budgétaires, suivi par projet, comptabilité d'engagement et de trésorerie, normes de reporting bailleurs, ingénierie pédagogique, gestion de projet.
Vous avez un niveau Excel avancé et maitrisez le fonctionnement d'un ERP.
Vous avez des compétences en business intelligence (Power BI, Power Query).
Vous êtes pédagogue et vous avez de bonnes capacités de communication et de résolution de problème.
Travaillant dans un environnement international, vous maîtrisez l'anglais à l'oral comme à l'écrit.

Conditions d'emploi

Statut : Cadre Intégré - CDD de remplacement de 4 mois - Temps plein
Lieu : Montreuil (Seine-Saint-Denis)
Rémunération : De 46K à 55Keuros bruts annuels sur 13 mois selon expérience
Avantages:25 jours par an de CP et 21 jours de RTT

item.title: Mental Health Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) Lead - Jamaica
item.description:
Country: Jamaica
Organization: Americares
Closing date: 3 Oct 2026

Position Title: Mental Health Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) Lead, Jamaica
Department: Regional Programs - Americas
Location: Jamaica

The position is mostly in-person with training and partnership work taking place at various organizations throughout the country. The position will also be based from home, with regular communication and collaboration with HQ and other teams remotely. The position is expected to travel within Jamaica 50% of the time, including to locations impacted by disasters. Some work will take place on weekends/outside of business hours during the contract year.

Key Relationships:
Reports to: Senior Manager, LAC
Direct Reports: 2
Assignment Type: Full-time, one-year contract

About Americares:
Americares is a global health and disaster relief organization that helps people and communities around the world access health in times of disaster and every day. Each year, Americares reaches 85 countries on average, including the United States, with life-changing health programs, medicine, medical supplies and emergency aid. Americares is one of the world’s leading nonprofit providers of donated medicine and medical supplies. For more information, visit americares.org.

Global health starts with you!

Americares Values:
We create global community, treating people as they want to be treated.

We respond effectively and responsibly, putting plans into practice.

We embed ethics and equity in our work and workplace.

We are better together; partnership is at our core.

We ask and listen, to create sustainable solutions for a healthier tomorrow.

We commit to quality, growing and improving to ensure individuals and communities thrive.

Key Outcomes:
In the first 90 days, the role will:
Learn and live the Americares values.
Complete all required new hire onboarding trainings.
Understand and actively lead Americares policies, procedures, and guidelines.
Establish relationships with key government, health sector, and community partners.
Conduct psychosocial and programmatic needs assessments to inform implementation priorities and establish any safe and accountable risks.
Establish confidential referral and escalation pathways for participant concerns and needs.
Develop detailed workplans and launch MHPSS activities in alignment with grant objectives and ensuring safe and accountable best practices.
Partner with HQ teams to begin planning for an annual organizational event that will be taking place in Jamaica in 2027.
Supervise and orient MHPSS Officers and project personnel, providing training and accountability for policies, procedures, compliance, and safe and accountable programming.
Begin delivery of staff care, psychoeducation, and capacity-building activities.
Establish monitoring, reporting, and quality assurance systems for program implementation.

In the first 6 months, the role will:
Lead the full implementation of safe and accountable MHPSS programming across priority locations in Jamaica.
Strengthen partner capacity through trainings, mentorship, and Training of Trainers activities.
Ensure effective referral pathways and coordination mechanisms are functioning.
Monitor program performance and compliance, and make evidence-based adaptations to improve quality and reach.
Successfully support with the planning and implementation of an organizational large-scale event in Jamaica.
Represent Americares in relevant MHPSS and humanitarian coordination forums.
Contribute to program reporting, learning products, and strategic planning efforts.

In the first year, the role will:
Successfully oversee delivery of the Jamaica MHPSS program and achievement of key grant objectives.
Strengthen sustainable safe and accountable MHPSS capacity among healthcare workers, social service providers, and community partners.
Demonstrate measurable improvements in access to psychosocial support services and referral systems.
Ensure high-quality monitoring, reporting, compliance, and grant management throughout the project.
Integrate MHPSS approaches into broader Americares health and humanitarian programming and support future program development opportunities.

Duties and Responsibilities:
-Lead and manage implementation of Americares MHPSS program in Jamaica, ensuring compliance and best practices for this role and direct reports.
-Supervise, mentor, and support MHPSS staff, consultants, and partners, ensuring success in meeting objectives while also supporting their professional growth.
-Oversee delivery and quality assurance of psychosocial support services, trainings (including Psychological First Aid), and staff wellbeing initiatives.
-Manage partnerships, grants, budgets, workplans, and compliance requirements.
-Strengthen community engagement and referral pathways for mental health and psychosocial services, including outreach with partners and potential partners to deepen and widen impact and referral networks.
-Monitor program performance, analyze data, and contribute to reporting and learning activities.
-Represent Americares with government, partner, and coordination stakeholders and support integration of MHPSS into broader health programming.
-Ensure that the work of direct reports and the overall project align to Americares policies, procedures, and guidelines.
-Actively model and lead Americares values, work culture and mission.
-Engage in and contribute to team spaces with openness, global competencies, and a growth mindset.
-Lead a global work community that ensures safe and accountable workspaces and programming.
-Other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

Degrees and/or experience required for the role:
• Active MHPSS related licensure and good standing with the Jamaica Council of Professions Supplementary to Medicine (CPSM).
• Graduate degree in psychology, counselling, or directly related field.

These competencies are required for the role:
-Experience in and competencies aligned with designing, implementing, and supervising MHPSS interventions.
-Strong clinical and psychosocial support expertise, including trauma-informed and crisis intervention approaches.
-Demonstrated ability to lead trainings, mentorship, and capacity-building initiatives for health and community-based personnel.
-Impeccable judgment, especially in high stress and independent working environments.
-Prior success with oversight of grants, partnerships, workplans, and program compliance requirements.
-Ability to conduct psychosocial and programmatic needs assessments and adapt programming accordingly.
-Experience coordinating cross-functional teams and stakeholders across field and headquarters environments.
-Strong monitoring, reporting, and data-driven decision-making skills.

Unrestricted Jamaican work authorization is required for this role.

Additionally, our core competencies as an organization are:
Ownership and results
Communication
Problem solving
Equity and inclusion
Teamwork and conflict resolution
Leadership
Prioritization
Management
Strategy and planning
Decision making

These competencies are preferred but not required:
MHPSS experience in disaster, emergency and/or humanitarian settings.

What you can expect, if you move forward in the steps of the recruitment process:
Video interview in Microsoft TEAMS with People and Talent
Video interview in Microsoft TEAMS with hiring manager
Video MHPSS technical interview in Microsoft TEAMS with Director, MHPSS – Americas
Video interview in Microsoft TEAMS with a panel of internal stakeholders
Reference check
Offer!

Our code of conduct, organizational values, and policies and procedures help to safeguard the welfare of everyone working for and participating in Americares programs. Americares is committed to the prevention of all types of abuse, discrimination, harassment, and exploitation. Employment with Americares will be subject to appropriate screening, reference, credentials, and background checks. By applying to our organization, job applicants confirm their understanding of and consent to our procedures during recruitment, and to adhering to our values and commitment to safe and accountable workplaces and programs as an employee.

item.title: ASISTENTE DE DISTRIBUCIÓN - CARABOBO
item.description:
Country: Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of)
Organization: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
Closing date: 25 Sep 2026

Acted es una ONG internacional sin ánimo de lucro con sede en París, Francia con operaciones en más de 40 países a nivel mundial. La misión de Acted es aportar asistencia humanitaria inmediata a aquellos que se encuentren en situación de necesidad al mismo tiempo que genera oportunidades a largo plazo para un crecimiento durable. Acted opera en contextos de catástrofe natural, conflicto armado y crisis socioeconómica.

Actualmente, Acted está buscando un/a Asistente de Distribución para integrar nuestro equipo en la misión de Venezuela.

Bajo la supervisión del/de la Oficial de Distribución el/la Asistente de Distribucion apoyará y participará en todo el ciclo de entrega de asistencia humanitaria (kits de emergencia y NFI) en refugios temporales y comunidades tras el sismo. Sus funciones incluyen garantizar las medidas de seguridad, el control de multitudes y la verificación de beneficiarios en terreno, cumpliendo con los estándares de transparencia, calidad y normativas de la organización.

Funciones

Gestión de Distribuciones: Preparar, organizar y supervisar la entrega de artículos a beneficiarios elegibles, garantizando el cumplimiento de los criterios de selección, normativas de la organización y procedimientos operativos estándar.

Control de Terreno: Garantizar el orden, la seguridad y la correcta gestión operativa durante las jornadas de distribución. Incluye la verificación de beneficiarios, el armado de kits, la organización del flujo de personas y el control de multitudes, además del registro detallado, la recopilación de firmas y la documentación de las entregas en terreno.

Coordinación y Transición: Apoyar a socios locales, autoridades comunitarias y comités de beneficiarios en la organización de los procesos de distribución y facilitar la transferencia progresiva de capacidades y actividades.

Protección y Acceso Seguro: Velar por la inclusión y el acceso digno de grupos vulnerables, brindando atención prioritaria a personas con discapacidad, niñez, mujeres embarazadas, lactantes y adultos mayores en los puntos de distribución y atención.

Supervisión de Personal: Liderar la selección, supervisión diaria, capacitación y control de asistencia del personal temporal y trabajadores comunitarios, asegurando el cumplimiento de los objetivos operativos.

Perfil deseado

Requisitos

Obligatorios:

  • Título universitario.
  • Al menos 1 año de experiencia en logística o distribución de asistencia humanitaria, preferiblemente en ONG.
  • Sólidos conocimientos de Microsoft Excel para el manejo de bases de datos.
  • Capacidad de resolución de conflictos, control de multitudes y gestión del tiempo.

Competencias:

  • Alta capacidad de planificación, autonomía en terreno y atención al detalle en la supervisión de obras.
  • Orientación a resultados bajo cronogramas estrictos y capacidad para realizar tareas operativas diversas.
  • Comunicación asertiva en entornos multiculturales, manteniendo principios de transparencia y rendición de cuentas.

Condiciones

  • Contrato de prestación de servicios bajo la figura de Honorarios Profesionales durante 3 meses con posibilidad de renovación según disponibilidad presupuestaria y desempeño.
  • Lugar de trabajo: Oficina de Acted en Carabobo
  • Honorarios profesionales según la escala de la organización.
  • Prestación de servicios de forma presencial con traslados recurrentes a las zonas afectadas por el doblete sísmico.

https://forms.gle/1wbgtNCh8dHeV1JN6

Acted es una ONG internacional sin ánimo de lucro con sede en París, Francia con operaciones en más de 40 países a nivel mundial. Funciones

Control de Terreno: Garantizar la seguridad en el sitio, el control de multitudes, la verificación de beneficiarios y la recepción exacta de los insumos asignados durante las jornadas de distribución y entrega.

item.title: Project Manager_LN
item.description:
Country: Kenya
Organization: International Medical Corps
Closing date: 30 Sep 2026

Only applicants who are eligible to work in Kenya without employer provided sponsorship are eligible for this position.

https://pims.internationalmedicalcorps.org/

International Medical Corps has developed PIMS, a customizable and flexible primary health, pharmacy and inventory management automation system designed for the last mile of the supply chain. PIMS enhances operational efficiency, controls costs and improves patient care by reducing paperwork for healthcare providers and maintaining optimal inventory levels, even in challenging environments. The Project Manager will be working with a team of professionals across the US, Jordan, Croatia, Kenya, etc. to successfully acquire partners and vendors, implement PIMS, and ensure success for loyalty retention.

JOB SUMMARY: The Project Manager is responsible for leading a cross departmental team to fulfill project goals and objectives. This position is responsible for managing risk, quality and progress of projects to organizational standards, and ensures projects are completed on time, on budget, to quality standards, and within agreed scope. The projects will tend to be medium to high complex in nature, has multi-department to enterprise-wide impact, and require a medium to large body of project resources.

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential function with or without reasonable accommodation.

MAIN TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

• Define project scope, goals and deliverables that support business goals in collaboration with senior management and stakeholders.

• Effectively, communicate project expectations to team members and stakeholders in a timely and clear fashion.

• Liaise with project stakeholders on an ongoing basis.

• Set and continually manage project expectations with team members and other stakeholders.

• Plan and schedule project timelines and milestones using appropriate tools.

• Track project milestones and deliverables.

• Determine the frequency and content of status reports from the project team, analyze results, and troubleshoot problem areas.

• Define project success criteria and disseminate them to involved parties throughout project life cycle.

• Conduct project postmortems (i.e. lessons learned) and create recommendations reports to identify successful and unsuccessful project elements.

• Estimate the resources and participants needed to achieve project goals.

• Draft and submit budget proposals and recommend subsequent budget changes where necessary.

• Where required, negotiate with other department managers for the acquisition of required staff time.

• Determine and assess need for additional staff and/or consultants and make the appropriate recruitment if necessary, during project cycle.

• Direct and manage project development from beginning to end.

• Develop full-scale project plans and associated communications documents.

• Delegate tasks and responsibilities to appropriate project team members and staff.

• Identify and resolve issues and conflicts within the project team.

• Identify and manage project dependencies and critical path

• Develop and deliver progress reports, proposals, requirements documentation, and presentations.

• Proactively manage changes in project scope, identify potential crises, and devise contingency plans.

• Coach, mentor, motivate and supervise project team members and contractors, and influence them to take positive action and accountability for their assigned work.

• Build, develop, and grow any business relationships vital to the success of the project.

Perform other duties as assigned. The duties and responsibilities listed in this document are representative of the nature and level of work assigned and not necessarily comprehensive.

Job Requirements

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

• Typically, a Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering. Equivalent combination of relevant education and experience may be substituted as appropriate.

• Master of Business Administration is preferred

• 7+ years hands on experience in leading medium to highly complex department and/or enterprise projects spanning across multi-disciplined areas, including 3+ years working with manager or director level.

• Core Adept Capabilities: Project Management, Influence and Negotiate, Deliver Results, Think and Solve Problems

• Core Intermediate Capabilities: Manage and Develop People, Finance, Act with Integrity

• Industry Project Management Certification (e.g. PMP, Prince2)

• Ability to operate a personal computer and other standard office equipment.

• Intermediate to advanced proficiency in working with Microsoft Office Suite, project management software, diagram/process flow software, conference software, and statistical software.

• Strong troubleshooting and technical research abilities a must.

• Must demonstrate the ability to work in a high pressure, fast-paced environment.

• Must be able to effectively multi-task with complete follow through.

• Must be energetic, self-motivated, and flexible.

• Excellent interpersonal/communication/written/documentation skills.

• Must have the ability to communicate technical information to non-technical users.

POSITION DETAILS

Project Title: Blue Horizon: Ocean Relief through Seaweed Aquaculture

Location: Flexible

Preferred time frame: Two phased approach is proposed (see Scope section for details):

  • Phase 1: Inception period, desktop review, and initial recommendations. To begin as early as late October 2026 and end by late January 2027.
  • Phase 2: Continued data collection, site visits and delivery of remaining deliverables commence June 2027 and end July/August 2027.

Potential site visits: Seaweed farms in Philippines and Viet Nam

INTRODUCTION

World Wildlife Fund, Inc. (WWF) policies and procedures for all GEF financed full-sized projects require a midterm evaluation (MTE). The following terms of reference (TOR) sets out the expectations for the MTE for the project: Blue Horizon: Ocean Relief through Seaweed Aquaculture hereafter referred to as the “project.” The technical consultant selected to conduct this evaluation will hereafter be referred to as “evaluator.”

The project is funded by the Global Environment Facility (GEF) and implemented through WWF-US as the GEF Agency. The project is executed by three partners, namely: 1) SEAFDEC Project Management Unit (PMU); 2) Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) of the Philippines; and 3) Department of Fisheries and Surveillance (DFiS) of Viet Nam. The project aims to enhance environmental, social, and economic benefits by developing sustainable seaweed value chains. Seaweed captures carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus, which helps mitigate ocean eutrophication and acidification, as well as improves habitat for marine life.

This project is delivered through four key components. Under Component 1: Regional Approach and Capacity for Seaweed Value Chains in Southeast Asia, the project is developing plans, tools, and training to build capacity and support a regional enabling environment for seaweed aquaculture. Component 2 supports the enabling environment for seaweed aquaculture at the national level in the Philippines and Viet Nam. This includes mapping to ensure proper siting of sustainable seaweed farms, national-level planning, and regulatory frameworks. Component 3 targets barriers faced in seaweed value chains, including production, processing, and marketing. The project will work with farmers and cooperatives to pilot seaweed farms in novel and innovative areas, including offshore seaweed farms, which will serve as proof of concept for seaweed production. The project will integrate standards for safe seaweed production into these seaweed farms. The project will also support new processing initiatives to increase the value of raw seaweed for local farmers. Finally, under Component 4: Knowledge Management, Monitoring and Evaluation, and IW:LEARN, the project is undertaking knowledge sharing, communications, and monitoring and evaluation. As an International Waters project, project activities are monitored and communicated through multiple channels, including IW:LEARN. Regional activities (under Components 1 and 4) commenced on June 30, 2024 by SEAFDEC, while Components 2 and 3 have not yet started. In the Philippines, start-up activities commenced with BFAR, whereas in Viet Nam, a grant agreement with DFiS has not yet been signed. The project was initially intended to be a four-year initiative from 2024 to 2028. However, the implementation timelines for Components 2 and 3 are based on national approval processes and are commencing later than originally anticipated. As a result, additional time is required to ensure the full delivery of project outputs and outcomes, and the project is now expected to conclude in 2030.

For more information on the project, please visit: https://www.worldwildlife.org/our-work/funds/wwf-gef/projects/blue-horizon-ocean-relief-through-seaweed-aquaculture/

SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES

WWF is seeking an independent consultant to undertake a Midterm Evaluation (MTE) of the Project. The scope of the MTE will cover the WWF GEF financed components.

The primary objective of this evaluation is to assess the project’s progress midway through implementation to determine whether it is on track to achieve its intended end-of-project results. The MTE report should contain findings related to the criteria and cross-cutting areas described in Annex A and should result in lessons learned and actionable recommendations that can be applied during the remaining project period.

Given the different stages of implementation across the project components, with national-level work under Components 2 and 3 commencing later than the regional and coordination work under Components 1 and 4, the Midterm Evaluation (MTE) will be undertaken in two phases.

Phase 1 should provide recommendations focused on Components 1 and 4, as well as strengthening alignment of implementation timelines (at national PMUs), milestones, and reporting processes across the project, while identifying measures to support effective delivery of planned results.

Phase 2 will complete the full MTE once Components 2 and 3 have sufficient implementation experience to assess. This phased approach seeks to balance the need for Components 1 and 4 to benefit from timely evaluative feedback with the need for Components 2 and 3 to reach a sufficient level of implementation maturity to generate meaningful evidence and lessons.

EVALUATION APPROACH AND METHODS

The evaluation will adhere to the relevant guidance, rules and procedures established by WWF and align with guidance from the GEF Terminal Evaluation and Ethical Guidelines. The evaluation must provide evidence‐based information that is independent, participatory, transparent, and ethical. The evaluator must be unbiased and free of any conflicts of interest with the project. The evaluator is expected to reflect all stakeholder views and follow a participatory and consultative approach. There should be close engagement with government counterparts, the GEF operational focal points in each country, the Executing Agency project management unit (PMU), partners and key stakeholders. Contact information will be provided.

The evaluation will use a mixed methods approach, drawing on both qualitative and quantitative evidence from secondary and primary sources. At a minimum, methods should include a desk review of project documents and available monitoring data, together with primary data collection in-country through key informant interviews, focus group discussions, and surveys. Please disclose any planned use of AI in the evaluation methodology and note that AI-generated report content is not permitted.

The evaluator will refine the methodological design during the inception phase and present a clear evaluation matrix linking evaluation questions, indicators of inquiry, data sources, and data collection methods. The final methodology should ensure appropriate coverage of all major stakeholder groups, including the PMU, Executing Agency, executing partners, government counterparts, GEF Operational Focal Points, and relevant stakeholders across the project geographies. The sampling approach should be gender responsive, socially inclusive, and suited to the project’s multi country and multi-level nature. A full list of stakeholders with contact details will be provided at inception.

The evaluation must triangulate findings across multiple methods and data sources. It should make systematic use of existing project documentation and monitoring information, while also assessing the quality and adequacy of that evidence. The evaluator should clearly identify and explain any methodological limitations, data gaps, or constraints affecting the analysis.

The Evaluation process will include the following, with deliverables in English marked by “*”:

Phase 1. Formative Review

Timeline: October 2026 to January 2027.

Purpose: Review progress and provide recommendations focused on Components 1 and 4, as well as on strengthening alignment of implementation timelines, milestones, and reporting processes across the project.

  1. Kickoff meeting;
  2. Desk review consisting of, but not limited to:
    • Project Document and CEO Endorsement Letter;
    • M&E Plan
    • Knowledge Management and Communication Strategy
    • Relevant safeguards documents, including the Safeguards Screen and Categorization memo, and the Stakeholder Engagement Plan;
    • Annual Work Plans (AWP) and Budgets;
    • Project Progress Reports (PPR) including Results Framework and AWP Tracking;
    • Gender Action Plan
    • GEF Agency reports, including Project Implementation Reports (PIRs) and Supervision Mission Reports (PrISM or BTORs);
    • Relevant technical deliverables
    • Relevant financial documents, including financial progress reports; co-financing monitoring tables and co-financing letters;
    • Meeting minutes (Project Steering Committee (PSC) and relevant virtual meetings with the WWF- GEF Agency and support team; and
    • Project Activities Reports (SEAFDEC PMU)
    • Other relevant documents provided by the Executing Agency and partners.
  • Inception Workshop to agree on approach and methods used;
  • Inception report (draft and final version) that outlines evaluation methodology*, which shall include data sources and data collection procedure, initial list of partners and stakeholders to be contacted for visits and interviews, revised timeline, survey tools or questionnaires to be utilized, Evaluation Matrix with guiding questions, etc.;
  • Interviews and discussions with Project Steering Committee (PSC) Members, Seaweed Technical Working Group (STWG), PMU and AMU; and
  • Delivery of Initial Recommendations report* with emphasis on Components 1 and 4 and aspects pertaining to alignment of timelines/reporting across all components of the project and aligning implementation timelines. Reviewed by PMU and WWF-US/ GEF Agency Discussion and action plan to follow during PSC meeting in February.

Phase II. Full Midterm Evaluation

Phase 2 will commence once Components 2 and 3 have achieved sufficient implementation maturity to allow assessment of progress toward outcomes. The anticipated timing is June through July/August 2027, subject to confirmation by WWF GEF Agency.

  • Kickoff, review and methodological update of Inception Report.
  • Desktop Review of new and updated documents, especially those related to Components 2 and 3.
  • Site visits in Philippines (Palawan and Zamboanga) and Viet Nam (Khanh Hoa and area to be determined) to meet with project parties and observe progress;
  • Interviews, discussions and consultations (virtual and/or in-person, as preferred) with WWF GEF Agency, PMU and executing partners, GEF Operational Focal Points (OFP), Project Steering Committee (PSC) members, beneficiaries, ASEAN Seaweed Technical Working Group (STWG), SEAFDEC/AQD, Global Seaweed Coalition, IW/LEARN, and others to be specified.
  • Presentation* of initial findings to WWF-US (GEF), PMU and others as specified;
  • Draft report* not to exceed 50 pages (excluding annexes) shared with GEF AMU, PMU, PSC, BFAR, DFiS National Focal Points, and OFPs for review and feedback. Note: The evaluator is expected to author the report; the use of artificial intelligence to generate report content is not permitted. Feedback log required for subsequent revisions. A sample outline will be provided; and
  • Final MTE report* that has incorporated comments, feedback log and data collected from the evaluation.

EXPECTED CONTENT OF EVALUATION REPORT

The Midterm Evaluation report will include:

  • Information on the evaluation process, including when the evaluation took place, sites visited, participants, key questions, summary of methodology and rating rubric, and feedback log showing how comments on draft were incorporated;
  • Assessment of Relevance, including project design and theory of change;
  • Assessment of Coherence;
  • Assessment of Effectiveness, including validation of midterm indicator measurements, progress toward outcomes, likelihood of achieving end-of-project results, and potential for results and impact;
  • Rating of individual outcomes and overall rating based on relevance, coherence, effectiveness, progress toward outcomes, and likelihood of achievement by project completion;
    • Assessment and rating of risks to the Sustainability of project outcomes;
  • Assessment and rating of Monitoring and Evaluation design and implementation, including the adequacy of adaptive management and use of evidence for course correction;
    • Assessment of knowledge management approach, including activities and products;
    • Assessment of replication and catalytic effects of the project;
    • Assessment of stakeholder engagement and gender-responsive measures;
    • Assessment of any environmental and social impacts and safeguards used for the project. A review of risk category classification and mitigation measures;
    • Assessment of Efficiency, financial management and summary of co-financing delivered;
    • Assessment of Implementation and Execution;
    • Summary rating tables, including justification and/or indicators for their determination;
    • Key lessons tied to identified strengths or issues;
    • Recommendations that include practical and short-term corrective actions by evaluation criteria to address issues and findings; and best practices towards achieving project outcomes, and knowledge sharing / replication for other projects of similar scope. See under Scope and Process headings for the phasing of these recommendations.

QUALIFICATIONS OF EVALUATOR(S)

Required Qualifications and Experience

  • Minimum eight years of relevant professional experience related to project monitoring, evaluation and learning.
  • Previous experience with evaluation methodologies
  • Excellent written and oral communication in English.

Preferred Qualifications and Experience

  • Recent experience conducting evaluations (for large/multilateral donors is an advantage);
  • Technical knowledge coastal/marine management, blue economy, fisheries or aquaculture value chains (especially seaweed value chains), or related field a plus;
  • Familiarity with GEF and related M&E policies. GEF project evaluation experience is an advantage over general GEF project development or implementation experience;
  • Experience with gender and social inclusion, participatory techniques, and review of gender policies;
  • Knowledge and experience in implementing or reviewing application of social and environmental safeguards policies in GEF (or similar) projects;
  • Regional experience an asset;
  • Experience with WWF/Conservation Standards, or theory of change approaches; and
  • Fluent Filipino/Tagalog and/or Vietnamese, OR translation services hired for interviews an advantage.
  1. ^For additional information on evaluation methods adopted by WWF, see the WWF Evaluation Guidelines, published on our WWF Program Standards public website.
  2. ^See GEF Terminal Evaluation Guidelines for additional information.
  3. ^Please see the GEF Ethical Guidelines as published on GEF website.
  4. ^Timeline to be revisited during evaluation based on progress in Philippines and Viet Nam.

For more details: see BH Seaweed_WWF Midterm Evaluation TOR _official.docx

How to apply

Interested consultants are invited to submit a technical and financial proposal in English (maximum 20 pages). The package should also include a curriculum vitae for each team member, where applicable, and a relevant writing sample, such as an evaluation report. Three people and their contact information should serve as professional references for the lead evaluator and/or report author; these references will only be contacted during the shortlisting phase of recruitment. Only complete proposals will be accepted. The financial proposal should be all-inclusive, including taxes, fees, and reimbursable expenses, if applicable. The total budget shall not exceed USD $45,000 Individual, team, or consulting firm proposals are welcome. Women and members of social minorities are encouraged to apply.

Interested consultants are requested to send their proposals to EvaluationsWWFGEF@wwfus.org by October 12, 2026. All questions about the requirements or process should be submitted to this email address by October 1, 2026. Responses to frequently asked and submitted questions will be available to all interested consultants at link (Annex G) until the application deadline.

The technical proposal and qualifications/experience of the individual or team will account for 90% of the weighted score of the proposal. The technical score will be based on how the proposal reflects an understanding of the work and adherence to the TOR and quality of the proposal (readability, depth/breadth and suitability of the methodology), as well as the degree to which the candidate meets desired and required qualifications/experience mentioned in the terms of reference above. The financial elements of the proposal will account for 10% of the weighted score of the application.

Once all proposals have been scored by the review committee, a shortlist of proposals will be determined, and the candidates notified. Please contact above email address if you have not received notification within two weeks of the deadline. In addition to having their referees contacted, shortlisted candidates will have their proposal reviewed by project stakeholders and will participate in an interview.

The selection process will be in compliance with WWF and GEF requirements. Any questions or concerns about non-compliance or irregularities in the process can be raised through WWF’s mechanism for reporting concerns available here: https://wwfus.ethicspoint.com.

Country: Ukraine

Closing date: 20 Oct 2026

Desired start date: ASAP
Duration of the mission: 5 months
Location: Kyiv

SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI) is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

ABOUT THE MISSION

Since the beginning of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine by Russian forces, SI has been responding to the needs of the population living in areas under Government control. While programming in 2022 and 2023 was—rightly—focused on immediate emergency response, the year 2024 marked a transition toward a more balanced approach, combining both emergency and early recovery interventions.
SI’s main strategic objective for 2026 is to strengthen and clearly position its comparative advantage in Ukraine. The ambition is for SI to build a recognized and demonstrable expertise in WASH and Shelter. The program strategy for 2026 therefore focuses on two core sectors—WASH and Shelter—and is structured around two strategic axes:
1. Respond to both acute and chronic emergencies
2. Contribute to creating the conditions for dignified return or sustainable stay in stable areas through a recovery-oriented approach
To maximize the impact of its interventions, SI aims to further enhance sectoral integration and promote localized approaches.
In 2026, SI’s country program in Ukraine is expected to operate with a budget of approximately 10 million euros, with three field bases (Mykolaiv, Dnipro, Kharkiv), one coordination office in Kyiv, and a total of 110 staff, including around 15 expatriates.
The main donors in 2026 are CDCS, AFD, and ECHO. Additional donors have been approached to expand and diversify the portfolio further, in line with SI’s programmatic priorities.

ABOUT THE JOB

SIZING OF THE TEAM ON THE BASE / IN COORDINATION :

Direct report to Country Director
Functional link with Field Coordinators and Field Coordinator Assistants
Direct line management of Deputy Access and Liaison Coordinator and Fire Safety officer
SI in Ukraine is composed of about 15 expatriates and 90 national staff

GENERAL OBJECTIVES :

On behalf of the Country Director, the Head of Security and Humanitarian Department oversees the definition of access, safety and security strategies, as well as the implementation of information gathering, analysis and the necessary frameworks, both at base level and in coordination.
They support the development of a network of reliable information and key contacts. They ensure compliance with the overall SI regulatory framework in their area and ensures the proper implementation of the Minimum Operational Standards for Security and Access.

ISSUES AND SPECIFIC CHALLENGES :

Static frontline but dynamic and volatile security context
Increasing range of drones, systemic targeting of critical infrastructures and logistical nods and massive attacks in areas of presence
Decreasing humanitarian access and challenged humanitarian principles

PRIORITIES ON THE 2-3 FIRST MONTHS :

Contribute to SI's access strategy in Sumy oblast and Kherson city, if applicable
Maintain a high level of standard in security management throughout the Country program, regardless of HR turnovers and gaps
Ensure dynamic risk assessments despite the routine
Participate to the capacity-building of local partners

SECURITY CONSTRAINTS :

Existing curfew from 01 am to 05 am
Frequent massive attacks targeting Kyiv
Daily drones presence leading to air alarms and often, the need to shelter
Adaptability of both sides to the conflict leading to frequent adaptative measures required

YOUR PROFIL

DIPLOMAS : Master in a humanitarian or security-related field

EXPERIMENT IN THE HUMANITARIAN SECTOR : more than 5 years

EXPERIMENT ON SIMILAR POSITIONS : 3-4 years

TECHNICAL SKILLS :

-Knowledge of standard corpus of security tools and documents in a country security pack

-Risk assessment and mitigation

-Staff training, development, coaching, and mentoring expertise

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS :

-Leadership and decision-making capacity

-Ability to work under pressure in a volatile security environment

-Strong inter-personal and analytical skills

LANGUAGES :

-English is Mandatory

-Ukrainian or Russian is a strong asset

SI WILL OFFER YOU

A salaried position:
According to experience, starting from EUR 2860 gross per month (2600 EUR base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of EUR 700.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

Breaks: During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

Insurance package: Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

How to apply

Do you recognise yourself in this description? If yes, please send us your CV and cover letter! https://www.solidarites.org/fr/depuis-1980/travailler-avec-nous/offres-emploi/deposer-votre-candidature/?jobId=PA3FK026203F3VBQB6G8N8NVU-116768&langCode=fr_FR

Please note that CV-only applications will not be considered, and that the vacancy may close before the deadline.

Thank you for your understanding.

BACKGROUND:

Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. The IRC is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief, relocating refugees and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster. Through 29 regional offices in cities across the United States, the IRC helps refugees resettle and become self-sufficient. Our programs are designed to ensure refugees thrive in America--whether ensuring children are enrolled in school, adults become self-reliant through employment or starting businesses, or families receive acute medical care they need to recover from trauma or illness. IRC Wichita has been assisting refuges since 2011. The Wichita office offers a range of services including trauma-informed family support, economic empowerment, education for youth and adults and immigration services. The IRC helps those in need to rebuild their lives and regain control of their future in their new home.

SCOPE OF WORK:

IRC believes that designing our strategies and programs based on clients’ particular needs and preferences is one of the most critical drivers of impact. We also believe that we have a role to play in working with clients so that they can engage as an equal, influential partner both with IRC and in the broader community through advocacy. The Client Voices Promoters will play a key role in supporting client engagement, and feedback initiatives at the local level. Promoters will work to bring together multi-ethnic, multi-racial and multi-sector constituencies to build the power of refugees and immigrants and the organizations that serve them to ensure their sustainability and improve people’s lives.

Working Environment:

Professional Standards: All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

US Benefits: We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

Project HOPE is an international NGO with more than 1,000 engaged employees and volunteers who work around the globe, responding to the world’s most pressing global health challenges. Throughout our 60-year legacy, Project HOPE has treated millions of patients, provided more than $3 billion worth of medicines to local health care organizations around the world helped build hundreds of health programs from the ground up, and responded to humanitarian crises worldwide.

Code of Conduct

It is our shared responsibility and obligation to treat each other with respect, take affirmative steps to prevent matters involving Sexual Exploitation & Abuse and Trafficking in Persons, and to disclose all potential and actual violations of our Code of Conduct, which may include Conflicts of Interest, Fraud, Corruption, Discrimination or Harassment. Together we can reinforce a culture of respect, integrity, accountability, and transparency.

SUMMARY:

Project HOPE is seeking an experienced Emergency Response Training Consultant to support the planning, design, and facilitation of a 2.5-day emergency response training for HQ support departments and country program leads.

The consultant will help translate Project HOPE’s emergency response framework, processes, and lessons learned into an engaging and practical learning experience. The training will strengthen participants’ understanding of emergency response roles and responsibilities, coordination between HQ and country programs, decision-making, and operational processes during an emergency.

PURPOSE:

The consultant will work closely with the Director of Emergency Preparedness and Response and the Emergency Response Unit to develop and facilitate a practical, engaging training.

The training will combine presentations, case studies, and tabletop simulations. Project HOPE’s Emergency Response Unit will lead the core training content, while the consultant will support the overall training design and facilitate the case studies and simulations.

SCOPE OF CONSULTANCY

The consultant will provide services in the following areas:

  • Develop the overall training and exercise design, including learning objectives, agenda, methodology, and participant materials.
  • Review relevant Project HOPE emergency response policies, procedures, tools, and lessons learned.
  • Support the development of training materials in coordination with Project HOPE staff.
  • Design realistic emergency scenarios, case studies, and tabletop exercises.
  • Develop facilitator guides, participant instructions, scenario injects, decision points, and debrief questions.
  • Facilitate tabletop simulations, breakout discussions, and plenary sessions.
  • Capture key lessons, coordination challenges, information gaps, and recommendations from the exercises.
  • Work collaboratively with Project HOPE staff throughout the planning, preparation, and delivery of the training.

EXPECTED OUTPUTS

During the consultancy period, the consultant is expected to deliver and support the following:

  • Training and exercise design plan
  • Training materials and supporting resources
  • Emergency response scenarios and tabletop exercise package
  • Facilitator and participant materials
  • Facilitation of the simulation sessions
  • Summary of key lessons and recommendations

Detailed deliverables, timelines, and expectations will be outlined in the consultancy Statement of Work.

TIMELINE

The anticipated consultancy timeline is:

  • October 1–14, 2026: Inception and planning
  • October 15–31, 2026: Training and exercise design
  • November 1–14, 2026: Final preparation and materials development
  • November 30–December 2, 2026: Training delivery

DURATION OF CONSULTANCY/ ESTIMATED LEVEL OF EFFORT:

Approximately up to a maximum of 20 consulting days.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

The ideal consultant will have:

  • Bachelor’s degree in international development, humanitarian studies, emergency management, public health, education, organizational development, or a related field. Advanced degree preferred.
  • Minimum 7 years of progressively responsible experience in humanitarian emergency response, emergency preparedness, crisis management, training and facilitation, or a related field, with demonstrated experience in emergency response training or exercise design.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and facilitating emergency response training, tabletop exercises, simulations, or scenario-based learning.
  • Experience working in or supporting emergency response operations, including coordination across multiple functions, departments, or country programs.
  • Experience developing adult learning materials, training curricula, case studies, and facilitated exercises.
  • Strong understanding of humanitarian response principles, emergency coordination, and decision-making in complex environments.
  • Experience working with international NGOs (INGOs), humanitarian organizations, international development organizations, or similarly complex global organizations.
  • Demonstrated ability to facilitate sessions with multidisciplinary teams and senior-level participants.
  • Excellent written, verbal, facilitation, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with organizational stakeholders and translate complex emergency response concepts into practical and accessible training.

The consultancy fee will be determined based on the scope of services, qualifications, and experience of the selected consultant.

Notice to applicants: Project HOPE does not conduct direct solicitation/recruitment via email. Project HOPE never asks consultant applicants for payment or financial information at any stage of the recruitment process. Project HOPE will never send you a third-party check and ask you to cash it. If you have been recruited via email, please contact Compliance@projecthope.org

Due to the substantial number of inquiries we receive, only applicants who meet the required qualifications and experience for this consultancy will be contacted. No phone calls please. However, since we are active around the world in the field of public health, we may wish to retain your CV in our database for other/future opportunities, unless you direct us otherwise.

Thank you very much for your interest in Project HOPE.

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

Our Kenya program, founded in 2006, operates under the local brand Tupande. Close to 500 staff in our Kakamega headquarters support 1,747 field staff and serve more than 1 million farmers. In Nairobi, around 50 staff support global functions like procurement, recruitment, government relations, and communications.

About the Role

The Export Logistics Specialist oversees and manages end-to-end export operations to ensure that goods leave the organization’s facilities and reach international vendors on time, within budget and in full compliance of all agreed regulations; including safety standards.

The role is focused on planning, coordination, documentation & stakeholder management for all exports handled by Soko.

Responsibilities

Export Operations & Coordination

  • Plan, organize, and oversee the entire export process from order placement to delivery at the destination.
  • Coordinate with production, warehousing, and procurement teams to ensure accurate and timely order fulfillment.
  • Liaise with freight forwarders, carriers, and third-party logistics providers to schedule shipments.
  • Track shipments, resolve delays, and ensure smooth cargo movement.

Documentation & Compliance

  • Prepare and review all required export documentation (invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, certificates of origin, export licenses, etc.).
  • Ensure compliance with international trade laws, customs regulations, and organizational policies.
  • Maintain accurate records of shipments for audit and reporting purposes.
  • Stay updated on changes in export/import regulations, customs procedures, and trade agreements.

Customer & Stakeholder Management

  • Act as the primary point of contact for clients regarding export logistics inquiries.
  • Provide timely updates to customers on order and shipment status.
  • Resolve customer complaints, shipment issues, or documentation errors promptly.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with shipping agents, port authorities, and regulatory agencies.

Performance Management

  • Negotiate shipping rates and terms with carriers and freight forwarders to optimize costs.
  • Analyze export logistics performance and recommend process improvements for efficiency and cost savings.

Reconditioning

  • Support and coordinate container reconditioning logistics when overseas regulators identify non-compliance issues.
  • Ensure all reconditioning processes follow approved SOPs and documentation standards before goods are released to buyers.
  • Maintain close communication with third-party service providers managing sterilization or product rework.

Supply Chain Traceability

  • Ensure all exported goods have a clear, verifiable origin and traceable supply chain documentation.
  • Work with sourcing and quality teams to build systems that enable end-to-end traceability of export products.
  • Maintain audit-ready export documentation, certifications, and inspection records in compliance with global regulatory standards.

Cost efficiency

  • Monitor freight costs, customs duties, and tariffs to control budgets.
  • Identify opportunities for cost reduction across shipping, warehousing, and handling processes.
  • Implement strategies that improve container utilization, reduce demurrage/detention, and optimize route planning.
  • Regularly review freight spend and propose cost-saving initiatives without compromising quality or timelines.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

  • 5+ years of experience in Supply chain, with at least 3 years focusing on Exports.
  • Proficiency in export management systems and tracking tools.
  • Proficiency in building complex formulas and functions in Google Sheets to support data analysis and reporting.
  • Language requirement: English is required. Working knowledge of Swahili is also useful
  • Strong planning and organizational skills.

item.description:
Country: Syrian Arab Republic
Organization: REACH Initiative
Closing date: 6 Oct 2026

Assignment

The IMPACT/REACH Syria mission, present in Damascus since 2025 and with activities in Syria since 2012, has traditionally had finance support from both the Acted Syria mission as well as dedicated IMPACT/REACH support in Amman. Since a shift in activities and location to Damascus, IMPACT/REACH is in the process of setting up a more independent finance structure to support activities in Syria. As such, IMPACT/REACH is looking for an experienced Senior Finance Officer, with ability to lead and advise on financial priorities, think critically about and manage financial workflows, meet financial deadlines, and oversee relevant finance staff.

Prior experience in managing finances for NGOs is essential, including budget development (with ability to proactively consult relevant team members to develop a high quality budget), financial reports, budget follow up (with ability to analyze and forecast spending, as well as advise senior management on financial decisions), and financial allocations and transactions. We are looking for someone who has an excellent finance background with experience in use of Excel and financial management software, and an ability to think creatively, lead independently, and advise senior managers in making wise financial decisions.

Under the supervision of the IMPACT Country Representative and the IMPACT Regional Finance Manager, the Senior Finance Officer is responsible for all financial tasks related to supporting the IMPACT/REACH Syria mission.

OBJECTIVES

Provides leadership to the IMPACT/REACH Syria finance team in ensuring that financial workflows are established, efficient, and effective

Acts as a senior advisor to the IMPACT/REACH senior management in ensuring that financial decisions are based on accurate, up-to-date financial information

Ensures that all financial budgeting and reporting deadlines are met on time

Works closely with Acted Syria finance and IMPACT regional finance to ensure that all financial processes are followed according to compliant procedures

FUNCTIONS

General financial management and leadership

  • Supports IMPACT/REACH management as relevant in coordinating finance-related activities with relevant stakeholders, and provides guidance in setting objectives and implementing workflows that allow the team to be efficient and effective
  • Conducts regular financial analysis and updates and advises IMPACT Country Representative on key financial decisions, including highlighting spending status and offering solutions if needed
  • Contributes to the development of financial strategies to optimize profitability and minimize risks
  • Acts as focal point for coordinating inputs or submission to Acted and IMPACT senior management and HQ teams in a timely manner and independently without requiring follow up, may manage 1-2 additional finance staff

Budget management

  • In coordination with the IMPACT CR, IMPACT RFM, and Acted CFM, lead in the preparation of budget proposals based on allocation tables, forecasting, and consultations with relevant program and finance teams
  • Ensure that budgets are submitted on time, quickly, and are presented in both internal format and converted accurately into donor formats when required
  • Follow up on validation of budget and make changes to budget as required by HQs or country management
  • Check, manage, and follow up on project follow up documents on a monthly basis to ensure that spending and financial allocations match the allocation tables
  • Lead in updating monthly allocation tables, timesheets, and running cost tables on time and accurately, in coordination with program, operations, and finance teams on spending plans

Accounting management

  • Ensure all financial and accountancy procedures are implemented and respected at the area level
  • Check the coherence of the cashbook, saga, and cash balance before closing the accountancy for each week and the end of each month
  • Ensure that all documentation (programmatic, procurement, or otherwise), is as per policy and in accordance with external donor regulations, before preparing any financial payments

Financial reporting

  • In coordination with relevant focal points, ensure that monthly follow up reports are completed accurately and on time
  • Close accurately the final expenditure report and ensure its adherence to the project plan before sharing with HQ for final reporting
  • Prepare accurately and in a timely manner all financial reports in the correct donor format and coordinate validation and approval from all stakeholders within Acted and IMPACT

Reporting and audit support

  • Ensure financial oversight and ensure that all IMPACT processes are compliant with audit processes
  • Attend audits as requested by Acted finance and compliance team and be prepared to lead on accurate responses regarding IMPACT finances
  • Prepare IMPACT inputs and coordinate with IMPACT HQ to provide inputs as requested by Acted finance team in preparation for audit

Other financial tasks

Support on any other financial task related to IMPACT Syria’s financial health

KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS

  • Accurate and on time financial analysis provided monthly to senior management
  • Accurate and on time budgets are prepared in coordination with country teams
  • Accurate and on time reporting and follow up processes are executed each month
  • Proactivity and leadership in ensuring finance tasks are executed at high quality

QUALIFICATIONS

  • University degree in accounting, finance, economics, business administration or equivalent
  • At least 4 years of experience progressively managing financial tasks and analysis required
  • Strong leadership skills in financial management and analysis
  • Excellent knowledge of excel, word, and outlook
  • Familiarity with accounting software (e.g. 1C; SAGA, QuickBooks)

Country: Switzerland

Closing date: 11 Oct 2026

Join MSF OCG as a HRIS Product Owner!

We are looking for passionate candidates ready to contribute to our humanitarian mission.

Below, you will find the job details and the qualifications we are looking for.

Inclusivity and Diversity at MSF

Do your qualifications and experience not exactly match all requirements of the job?

At MSF OCG, we are committed to an inclusive culture that supports and amplifies the diverse voices of our staff members. We strive to create workplaces where teams of people with diverse backgrounds, characteristics, perspectives, ideas and experiences work together to advance MSF's social mission and create better outcomes for our patients and the communities we work with.

We understand that some people may hesitate to apply for employment if they don't meet all listed job requirements. Research shows that this is especially true for women. If you believe your profile is a good match for this position, we invite you to apply even if you don’t fulfil every listed qualification.

We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment. All selected candidates will undergo reference checks.

Context & mission

Médecins Sans Frontières is an independent, international medical and humanitarian organization that provides care to people in need, people affected by natural or man-made disasters, and victims of armed conflict, without discrimination and without regard to race, religion, creed or political affiliation (MSF Charter).

The MSF movement is built around 5 operational centers supported by 24 sections and offices worldwide. MSF Operational Center Geneva (MSF OCG) is one of these centers.

The HRIS Product Owner leads the LIGO RUN (Workday) team and ensures stable, effective and user-centred HRIS services for OCG, in alignment with the OCG Strategy and broader HR Transformation objectives.

The role is responsible for service delivery, product ownership, roadmap and backlog management, activity as well as budget planning, team management, shared tenant collaboration and continuous improvement of LIGO / Workday, which was recently deployed within OCG.

As LIGO is a core pillar of OCG HR Transformation, the role translates strategic objectives into sustainable operational delivery, while progressively building the governance, capacity and ways of working required for long-term service continuity and a future transition under IT.

Tasks & Responsibilities

HRIS Service Delivery and Product Ownership

  • Act as Product Owner for LIGO from an OCG perspective, managing the roadmap and backlog in line with HR strategic priorities, user needs, operational requirements and shared tenant constraints.
  • Prioritise system evolutions, enhancements and corrective actions based on business value, service impact, feasibility, risks, resources and budget.
  • Ensure continuity, stability and quality of LIGO services across support, incident management, service requests, functional administration, integrations, releases, enhancements and continuous improvement.
  • Coordinate with HR stakeholders, user groups, IT, TMA (Tierce Maintenance Applicative) providers, global LIGO roles and other partners to ensure effective delivery and resolution of issues.

User Experience, Adoption, Data and Continuous Improvement

  • Ensure that user experience, adoption and change management are embedded in the design, delivery and evolution of LIGO services.
  • Oversee communication, training, user support, feedback collection and adoption activities to improve effective use of LIGO by HR teams, managers and employees.
  • Promote reliable, consistent and usable HR data, ensuring that data quality, reporting and downstream impacts are considered in system changes.
  • Support simplification, harmonisation, automation and improvement of HR processes through LIGO.
  • Monitor service performance, user feedback, recurring issues and improvement opportunities, and translate them into concrete actions.

Team Management and Capacity Building

  • Manage, organize and coordinate the multidisciplinary LIGO service delivery team, including HR functional referents, functional administration, IT business analysis, integration, support, user experience and adoption roles.
  • Define clear roles, responsibilities, priorities, ways of working and escalation paths within the team.
  • Plan and monitor workload, team capacity and delivery priorities across RUN, roadmap, support, adoption, integration, data and governance activities.
  • Support the professional development of team members and strengthen collective expertise, autonomy, documentation and knowledge sharing.
  • Build a collaborative team culture focused on service quality, accountability, user impact, continuous improvement and sustainable support.

Activity Planning, Resource and Budget Management

  • Lead annual and multi-year activity planning for the LIGO service delivery scope, translating HR Transformation priorities into operational plans, milestones and measurable outcomes.
  • Prepare, manage and monitor the LIGO service delivery budget, including internal resources, external support, TMA services, maintenance, enhancements, training and adoption activities, taking into account constraints (resource, budget, shared tenant).
  • Contribute to defining a sustainable resourcing and funding model for LIGO as the service matures and prepares for a future IT-based operating model.

Governance, Collaboration and Future Operating Model

  • Represent OCG in shared Workday tenant governance and contribute to a coherent, sustainable and collaborative operating model with other MSF entities, representing the broader OCG stakeholders
  • Define and promote clear ways of working for prioritisation, impact assessment, decision-making, releases, testing, tenant administration, data, security and change management.
  • Collaborate with IT, global LIGO roles, TMA (Tierce Maintenance Applicative) provider, HR stakeholders, user groups representatives and other application managers / product owners across the wider system architecture.
  • Prepare the progressive transition of LIGO service delivery from HR Transformation towards a future IT-based operating model, while preserving business proximity and HR strategic alignment.)

Your profile

Experience and Knowledge

  • Significant understanding of MSF, and/ or humanitarian settings constraints and operations centred service orientation mindset.
  • Significant experience in HRIS service delivery, product ownership, application management or HR transformation, ideally with Workday or another integrated HRIS.
  • Strong understanding of HR processes, HR operating models, digital HR services and post-go-live / RUN environments.
  • Experience leading multidisciplinary teams across business, functional, technical, support, user experience and adoption roles.
  • Experience in roadmap management, backlog prioritisation, stakeholder arbitration, activity planning, budget monitoring and resource management.
  • Good understanding of IT service management, application governance, integrations, data governance, security principles and multi-entity/shared system environments.
  • English and French are the working languages of MSF Switzerland.

Skills/ Technical competencies

  • HRIS service delivery and product ownership.
  • Team leadership, coordination and capacity building.
  • Activity planning, budget management and resource planning.
  • Prioritisation, decision-making and stakeholder arbitration.
  • Strong communication, facilitation, documentation and synthesis skills.

Personal Abilities/Qualities

  • Strategic and operational mindset.
  • Strong service orientation and user focus.
  • Collaborative leadership style.
  • Ability to create structure in a complex and evolving environment.

Languages

  • Fluent English and French required; other MSF working languages are an asset.

Terms of employment

  • Full-time position 100% (40h/week)
  • Fixed-term contract, until December 31st, 2027
  • Working place: Geneva, Switzerland
  • Ideal start date: As soon as possible
  • Gross annual salary (for 100%): from CHF 110’652.- to CHF 126’228.- (salary commensurate with equivalent experience and internal salary grid)
  • Paid vacation: 25 days per year, prorate temporis, plus any Swiss public holidays falling within the contract period.
  • Pension plan: pension contribution covered 3/4 by MSF, 1/4 by staff member.
  • Relocation support available for eligible candidates.

How to apply

Candidates are invited to submit their application exclusively through our recruitment platform, following these guidelines:

  • CV (maximum 2 pages)
  • Cover letter (maximum 1 page)
  • Documents must be submitted in either English or French.

The application deadline is October 11th, 2026.

We reserve the right to close this vacancy earlier if we receive a sufficient number of quality applications.

APPLY

All applications will be treated confidentially.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Please note that we do not wish to use the services of recruitment or placement agencies.
